name: Ask, approve, try it
intro: A client who is not an engineer asks for a CRM dashboard in plain words, approves twice, and 17 minutes later has working, tested software waiting for review. Every frame is from a real run on a real server.
facts: Request to merge request, approvals included
Words the client typed to approve
links: The factory, and how to run it

scenes.kicker: A software factory, for people who are not engineers
scenes.title:
Ask. Approve.
Try it.
scenes.say: A client asks for software in plain words. A factory of AI agents builds it, checks it, and shows it to them.
scenes.voice: Ask. Approve. Try it. This is a software factory, seen from the client's side: someone who is not an engineer asks for software in plain words, and gets it.

scenes.title: A factory, for software
scenes.define: Every request follows the same written pipeline. AI agents do the work, a second agent checks every piece, and a person approves at two moments.
scenes.voice: A software factory is a written pipeline that every request follows. AI agents do the work. A second agent checks every piece of it. And a person approves at two moments: before anything is built, and before it ships.

scenes.title: Three parts to play
points: Asks in plain words. Approves twice. Tries the result.
Writes down the request, plans it, builds it, checks it, puts it online.
Sets the factory up once. Decides what ships.
scenes.voice: Three parts to play. The client asks, approves, and tries the result. The factory writes the request down, plans it, builds it, checks it, and puts it online. Your team sets the factory up once, and decides what ships.

scenes.title: Ask in plain words
scenes.say: The client has a GitLab login and a project of their own.
scenes.voice: Chapter one. Ask.

scenes.title: Start from an empty app
scenes.say: Each client gets a private project. It starts as an empty page.
scenes.voice: Each client gets a private project of their own.

scenes.say: The client's app, before the first request
scenes.voice: This is their app today: an empty page, waiting for the first request. It sits behind a login only they have.

scenes.say: Their own private project in GitLab
scenes.voice: And this is their project in GitLab. They see this project, and nothing else on the server.

scenes.title: Ask for something
scenes.say: A new issue, written the way you would message a colleague.
scenes.voice: Step two: ask for something.

scenes.say: A title, and what they want, in their own words
scenes.voice: They open a new issue. The template asks two things: what should change, and how they will know it works. Here: a CRM dashboard, with customers in a table and totals at the top.

scenes.say: Filed. The factory label hands it over.
scenes.voice: They press Create. The template adds the factory label, and that hands the request over.

scenes.title: The factory writes it down
scenes.say: Nothing is built until the client agrees with what was understood.
scenes.voice: Chapter two. The factory writes it down.

scenes.title: It picks the request up
scenes.say: Within a minute, it says so on the issue.
scenes.voice: Step three: the factory picks the request up.

scenes.say: It reports each step on the issue as it goes
scenes.voice: Within a minute it comments on the issue: picked up, requirements written, and now waiting for a person. It reports every step like this, in the open.

scenes.say: Its turn is over. Now it is the client's.
scenes.voice: Then it stops, and says what it needs: read the requirements, and reply approve.

scenes.title: Read what it understood
scenes.say: The request, turned into stories with checks.
scenes.voice: Step four: read what it understood.

scenes.say: Requirements, written from the client's words
scenes.voice: An agent read the request and the code, and wrote it down as requirements.

scenes.say: Each story comes with checks it must pass
scenes.voice: Each story comes with acceptance checks. Every later stage is held to these, so the client is agreeing to something specific.

scenes.say: The status page: where it stands, and whose turn it is
scenes.voice: The client also has a status page. Plain words, five steps, and whose turn it is. Right now: theirs. One button opens the conversation.

scenes.title: Approve with one word
scenes.say: Reply approve. That is the whole interface.
scenes.voice: Step five: approve.

scenes.say: One word starts the build
scenes.voice: They reply with one word: approve. The comment starts the next pass straight away.

scenes.title: One builds, another checks
scenes.say: A maker builds each section. A separate checker verifies it.
scenes.voice: Chapter three. Build, and check.

scenes.title: Plan, build, check
scenes.say: Nothing moves on until a second agent says it passed.
scenes.voice: Step six: plan, build, and check.

scenes.say: The plan: sections, each ending in a check
scenes.voice: First, a plan. The work is split into sections, and each section ends in a check that can be run.

scenes.say: A maker builds. A separate checker verifies.
scenes.voice: One agent, the maker, builds a section. A different agent, the checker, verifies it. The checker never saw the maker work. If it fails, the work goes back with written findings.

scenes.say: The checker's evidence: what it ran, expected, and found
scenes.voice: The checker writes down its evidence: each check it ran, what it expected, and what it found. That evidence travels with the change.

scenes.say: Then the whole change is checked again, and put online
scenes.voice: Then the whole change is checked again, the tests run, and it is put online for the client to try.

scenes.title: Try it before it ships
scenes.say: The client uses the real change in a browser.
scenes.voice: Chapter four. Try it.

scenes.title: Use the change
scenes.say: A link to the change, running.
scenes.voice: Step seven: use the change.

scenes.say: The client's turn again, with a link to try it
scenes.voice: The factory stops again, and posts a Try it link.

scenes.say: The status page says so too
scenes.voice: The status page shows the same: built and checked, and their turn.

scenes.say: The CRM dashboard they asked for, running
scenes.voice: And here it is. The CRM dashboard they asked for, running in the browser. Built from one paragraph.

scenes.say: Totals at the top, every customer at a glance
scenes.voice: Totals at the top, and every customer at a glance. Just what the issue said, and what the requirements checked.

scenes.title: Approve again
scenes.say: Happy with it? One word again.
scenes.voice: Step eight: approve again.

scenes.say: The second and last approval
scenes.voice: Happy with it, they reply approve. That is the second and last thing they type.

scenes.title: Handed over, with proof
scenes.say: A merge request with the code, the tests, the specs and the evidence.
scenes.voice: Chapter five. Hand over.

scenes.title: A merge request opens
scenes.say: Merging stays a person's call.
scenes.voice: Step nine: a merge request opens.

scenes.say: Code, tests, specs and evidence, ready for review
scenes.voice: The factory opens a merge request: the code, the tests, the specs, and the checker's evidence, linked to the issue. A person on your team reviews it and merges it.

scenes.say: Done. Every step ticked.
scenes.voice: The status page shows it done, every step ticked, with links to the conversation, the change to try, and the finished work.

scenes.say: The whole history stays on the issue
scenes.voice: And the whole history stays on the issue: every step, every check, every approval, in one place.

scenes.title: One factory, many clients
points: Each client sees only their own GitLab project.
Each project gets a pipeline of its own.
Previews and a status page, behind their own login.
scenes.voice: One factory serves many clients. Each has their own project, their own pipeline, and their own previews and status page, behind their own login.

scenes.say: Adding a client is one command
scenes.voice: Adding a client is one command. It creates the project, the pipeline, the login, and the links to share.

scenes.title: Ask for a project
scenes.say: Get a project of your own, file a small request, and watch it get built.
scenes.voice: Want to try it? Ask for a project of your own, file a small request, and watch it get built.
